after_landing.notes: Archives the plan folder only when its gaps list has no open entry; with an open gap, skip this step and leave the folder live.

release_levels.reason: Every synced file gets the new header path once, so each consumer sees a one-time diff in each synced file. The consumer changes nothing by hand.

units.title: The move to repo/ and the header paths
Engine: one root for the repo tool folders
Tests: the repo/ layout
units.waits: Its cases copy the repo/ folder that U1 makes and run the engine paths that U2 changes.

shared_files.why: every human-facing doc; the earlier units report DOCS FALSIFIED lines and never edit a doc

decisions.decision: Does the plan need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U1 moves every shipped task script and changes the headers of runnable files, U2 changes the engine paths, and U3 changes a test task. All of them land runnable bash. One review unit in wave 3 covers U1, U2 and U3.
decisions.rejected: No review unit; the wave review alone does not run /security-review.

decisions.decision: Why is this plan in one linear chain with the other plans of the merge?
decisions.ruling: The 16 plans form one linear chain through requires. Most of them edit sync-engine/repo-sync or sync-engine/setup-sync, and parallel plans conflict there.

decisions.decision: Where do the tests of the new rules go?
decisions.ruling: This plan extends test:repo-sync with cases for its new rules. An existing case changes only where a ruling changes its expected result.

decisions.decision: Who runs mise run setup:configs in bootstrap and in the consumers?
decisions.ruling: The user, by hand, after the landing. It is out of scope, as in the earlier plans.
decisions.rejected: A unit or an after-landing step runs setup:configs.

decisions.decision: What happens to the forwarding file at tools/repo-sync/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/repo-sync?
decisions.ruling: It stays at its path, with its content and its header unchanged, until the parked cleanup plan. It is the only file left under tools/, and the sync no longer ships it, because the tool root is repo/tools. Old consumer stubs source it from the clone.
decisions.rejected: Remove it in this plan (old consumer stubs source it); move it to repo/tools (then the sync ships it again).

decisions.decision: What happens to the synced copy .config/mise/tasks/_scripts/repo-sync in a consumer?
decisions.ruling: Both hold. With a P05 manifest, the stale rule removes the consumer copy of .config/mise/tasks/_scripts/repo-sync, because the sync no longer ships it and nothing in a consumer sources it after P01. Without a manifest, the copy stays until the parked cleanup, whose migrate.md item covers it. docs/sync/tools/repo-sync.md says so; no migrate.md item in P06.
decisions.rejected: Keep the forwarding file shipped until the parked cleanup.

decisions.decision: Which path do the engine messages name?
decisions.ruling: Each message that names a tool file names the path in the clone, repo/tools/<tool>/<path>, and repo/packs.toml for the packs. The tests that compare these messages change their expected text.
decisions.rejected: Keep the old tools/<tool> text in the messages.

decisions.decision: The header bullet of the rulings shows tools/<side>/<tool>/<path>, and the later layout bullet shows repo/tools/<tool>/<path>. Which path does the header name?
decisions.ruling: repo/tools/<tool>/<path>. The layout bullet is later and names the header path explicitly.
decisions.rejected: tools/repo/<tool>/<path>, which the layout bullet rejects (not tools/repo/).

decisions.decision: Which paths does the example-review command name after the move?
decisions.ruling: git log <commit_id>..HEAD -- tools repo docs/sync CLAUDE.md. It keeps tools until commit_id is set again, because the contract changes before the move are under tools/. P15 later adds docs/design.
decisions.rejected: git log <commit_id>..HEAD -- repo docs/sync CLAUDE.md, which misses the changes before the move.

decisions.decision: What happens to the tools/packs.toml exclude that P04 adds to the root dprint.jsonc?
decisions.ruling: The exclude follows the file: P06 changes it to repo/packs.toml. The global dprint config sorts TOML keys (sortKeys: true), and the engine reads the pack members in file order.
decisions.rejected: Drop the exclude and let dprint sort the members, which reorders the tools and the hooks.
